questions.question: What is the method of preservation of biological material at very low temperature in liquid nitrogen?
questions.solution_html:
• What is the method of preservation of biological material at very low temperature
  • in liquid nitrogen?
  • Cryopreservation.
  • Cryopreservation is the technique of preserving biological materials (such as gametes,
  • embryos, tissues, or cells) at very low temperatures, typically in liquid nitrogen
  • (−196 °C) . At this temperature, all metabolic activities are completely halted ,
  • allowing long-term storage without damage.

questions.question: Descibe sexual dimorphism in crabs.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe sexual dimorphism in crabs
  • Abdomen shape: Male – narrow, triangular, Female – broad, rounded
  • Pleopods : Male – modified (copulatory), Female – well developed (egg carrying)
  • Chelipeds (claws): Male – larger, stronger, Female – smaller
  • Body size: Male – usually larger, Female – smaller (but broader abdomen)
  • Gonopores position: Male – on base of 5th walking legs , Female – on base of 3rd
  • walking legs
  • Abdominal segments: Male – fewer free segments , Female – more expanded for
  • brooding

questions.question: Describe oviparity, viviparity and ovoviviparity in fishes.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe oviparity, viviparity and ovoviviparity in fishes
  • Oviparity: Egg laying, Fertilization – external (mostly), Development – outside body ,
  • Large number of eggs, Less parental care
  • Viviparity: Live bearing , Fertilization – internal, Embryo develops inside female ,
  • Nourishment from mother, Fewer young, more protection
  • Ovoviviparity: Eggs retained inside female , Fertilization – internal, Development
  • inside egg within mother, Nourishment from yolk (no direct maternal supply) , Young
  • released as live

questions.question: Describe the procedure of hypophysation.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the procedure of hypophysation
  • Hypophysation (induced breeding using pituitary extract)
  • Selection of brooders – healthy, mature male & female , Collection of pituitary
  • gland – from donor fish , Preparation of extract – pituitary homogenized in
  • distilled water/saline , Dose determination – based on body weight & species
  • Injection – intramuscular/intraperitoneal, Two doses (female) : Preliminary
  • (priming) doseand Final (resolving) dose, Single dose (male) – at time of female’s
  • final dose , Latency period – time between injection & spawning , Spawning –
  • natural or artificial (stripping) , Fertilization – mixing eggs & milt , Incubation –
  • hatching of eggs under controlled conditions

questions.question: Describe the gonadal level of control in induced maturation and spawning. [6x5 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the gonadal level of control in induced maturation and spawning
  • Target organ – Gonads (ovary & testis)
  • Steroid hormones – Estrogens (e.g., estradiol) – vitellogenesis (yolk
  • formation), Androgens – spermatogenesis, Progestogens (maturation-inducing
  • hormone, MIH) – final maturation
  • Ovary – Oocyte growth, Vitellogenesis, Final oocyte maturation, Ovulation
  • Testis - Spermatogenesis, Sperm maturation, Spermiation
  • Maturation Inducing Hormone (MIH) – Triggers germinal vesicle breakdown
  • (GVBD), Leads to final oocyte maturation
  • Feedback control – Steroids regulate pituitary & hypothalamus

questions.question: Describe anaesthetics used in fish breeding and handling, their importance and methods of administering anesthetics. [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Describe anesthetics used in fish breeding and handling, their importance and
  • methods of administering anesthetics
  • Common anaesthetics used
  • MS-222 (Tricaine methanesulfonate) : Most widely used, Rapid action, safe
  • Benzocaine : Cheap, effective, Requires alcohol for dissolution
  • 2-Phenoxyethanol : No buffering needed, Stable in water
  • Clove oil (Eugenol) : Natural, low cost, Common in hatcheries
  • Quinaldine : Used in marine fishes
  • Importance / Uses: Reduces stress during handling, Prevents injury to fish & handler ,
  • Facilitates breeding operations
  • Stripping of eggs & milt , Artificial fertilization
  • Ease of transport , Accurate measurements (length, weight) , Tagging, surgery,
  • sampling, Improves survival rate, Minimizes metabolic activity
  • Methods of administration
  • Immersion (most common) : Fish placed in anaesthetic solution , Absorption
  • through gills
  • Dip method : High concentration, short duration
  • Prolonged bath : Low concentration, long exposure
  • Irrigation method : Anaesthetic water passed over gills, Used during surgery
  • Stages of anaesthesia
  • Light sedation → loss of equilibrium → deep anaesthesia → recovery
